title: Claude emerges as fastest-growing AI skill in Korean job postings
source_used: The Korea Times (full text, AMP page)
key_facts: JobKorea, an HR technology platform operated by Worksphere, released data on Monday 12 Oct 2026 showing job postings that mention generative AI tools such as Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini rose 170 percent in the third quarter from a year earlier.
By tool, mentions of Claude rose 770 percent, Google's Gemini 500 percent, ChatGPT 165 percent, Microsoft Copilot 96 percent and Midjourney 46 percent.
Claude's share of postings that name a specific AI tool rose from 17 percent to 55 percent; ChatGPT's share stayed around 70 percent.
Mentions of generative AI, prompt engineering, AI agents and vibe coding rose 235 percent year on year.
AI proficiency is also listed as a preferred qualification for marketing, sales and operations roles, not only software development.
Postings mentioning Microsoft Word fell 16 percent, computer skills certification 10 percent and Photoshop 9 percent, while Excel mentions rose 10 percent.
The share of postings that specify preferred academic majors fell to 6.5 percent in the third quarter, from 13.1 percent in the same period of 2021.
A JobKorea representative said employers increasingly want candidates who can apply specific AI tools in practical work; JobKorea's AI Jobs section lists more than 1,200 roles.
quote_evidence: Among individual tools, Claude recorded the sharpest increase, with mentions climbing 770 percent, followed by Google’s Gemini at 500 percent, ChatGPT at 165 percent, Microsoft Copilot at 96 percent and Midjourney at 46 percent.

Claude’s share of postings that named specific AI tools jumped from 17 percent last year to 55 percent this year, narrowing the gap with ChatGPT, whose share remained around 70 percent over the same period, according to JobKorea.
A Job Korea representative said employers increasingly want candidates who can apply specific AI tools in practical work as generative AI becomes part of everyday business operations.
why_it_matters_hint: Korean employers are moving from asking whether candidates understand AI to naming the specific tools they must use, which shapes what job seekers need to learn.
event_date: 12 Oct 2026 (data for the third quarter of 2026)
notes: Figures are JobKorea's own counts of mentions in postings on its platform. The Korea Times states the article was published with the assistance of generative AI and edited by the newspaper.
